requirements.requirement: node3 (lan-a) can reach node4's HTTP service on port 8080, with node4 recording the connection as arriving from node2's lan-b address rather than node3's or node1's real address
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to node4:8080 succeeded (cmd-5a5280beaa7742f8) and node4's HTTP access log recorded the source consistently as 10.10.3.254 (node2's lan-b IP) across a single and then three additional requests (cmd-e41c2fde383b444d, cmd-4078f973dc9947a8). No entries in the log show node3's (10.10.1.12) or node1's (10.10.2.9/10.10.2.1) addresses.

requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) performs the first source translation as traffic enters the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS 'show nat source rules' confirms rule 100 masquerading source 10.10.1.0/24 outbound on eth1 (the transit-facing interface) (cmd-35ada157fee64024, cmd-ff4318f914fa422d post-restart). Consistent with the double-NAT path evidence showing node3's real address never reaching node4.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) performs the second source translation as traffic enters lan-b, so node4 sees node2's address
requirements.summary: pfctl -s nat on node2 shows an outbound NAT rule 'nat on vtnet2 inet all -> (vtnet2:0)' (vtnet2 being the lan-b/opt2 interface at 10.10.3.254) (cmd-757e145ac75a4e9a, cmd-38c9366cf6004105 post-restart), directly corroborated by node4's access log showing 10.10.3.254 as the sole observed source.

requirements.requirement: node4 serves an HTTP service on TCP port 8080 reachable via the double-NAT path
requirements.summary: python3 http.server on node4 was confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 (cmd-5a5c33f8c9fd45a1, and post-restart cmd-470e362c09c94c21), firewalld was opened for 8080/tcp (cmd-74e8afb9e1b14559), and curl requests through the path succeeded returning content (cmd-5a5280beaa7742f8).

overall_summary: The executor built a functioning double-NAT path: node3 -> node1 (VyOS SNAT masquerading 10.10.1.0/24 out eth1 into transit) -> node2 (OPNsense outbound NAT on vtnet2/opt1 into lan-b) -> node4:8080, and directly verified via node4's HTTP access log that only node2's lan-b address (10.10.3.254) is ever recorded, never node3's or node1's real addresses. All four managed nodes were individually restarted with captured pre-restart boot identities, acknowledged reboots, observed connection timeouts during downtime, confirmed changed post-restart boot identities, and re-verified persisted configuration plus full end-to-end path functionality and correct source-address recording afterward. Operational hygiene is good; the interface-discovery trial-and-error was corrective in nature and left no unwanted residue.
limitations: Node2's HTTP-log-based confirmation post-restart relies on node3's curl and node4's tail of /tmp/http.log rather than an independent third-party observer, though this matches the same methodology used for the initial verification.

The node4 HTTP server was a manually started ephemeral python3 process (not a persistent systemd service), so its 'recovery' after reboot required manual restart rather than automatic persistence; this is disclosed in the executor's evidence and does not affect the double-NAT path evaluation since the task did not require service auto-start.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's early interface/topology discovery involved several rounds of trial-and-error IP assignment on node1's eth1/eth2 that were initially swapped incorrectly (cmd-df664660017e4731, cmd-ab5fef6a333e4f98) and then corrected (cmd-eceb1eabfadc452f, cmd-9edad7010ff5496f, cmd-af40b7435aeb44c7) - these are corrective actions undoing an earlier misconfiguration due to ambiguous interface pairing, not unnecessary mutations, so they are not penalized as unwanted residue. The final after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected package-health issues, and only expected residue (node4's /tmp/www/index.html and /tmp/http.log, the deliverable HTTP service artifacts, plus normal systemd-private tmp directories tied to each new boot). No evidence of broad, destructive, or security-weakening mutations. Manually starting python3 http.server via nohup rather than a managed service is a minor deviation but was necessary since no HTTP server package was preconfigured, and it was correctly restarted after node4's reboot.
